findings.title: Tab-spliced verifier TSV becomes forged SAFE(stale) authorization
findings.explanation: Quarantine drops two tab fields without validating the echoed path; tabs in a filename replace verdict and receipt. Both verifier JSON verdicts are NOT-SAFE, yet dry-run passes.
findings.recommendation: Consume structured JSON with validated fields, or reject record separators before invoking/parsing the engine.

findings.title: Hidden live references are missed by both stale verifiers
findings.explanation: The benign hidden consumer file contains the literal artifact basename. rg --no-ignore lacks --hidden, so both tools certify refs=0 and quarantine accepts stale.
findings.recommendation: Include hidden live-reference surfaces while retaining explicit protected-path and secret-content exclusions; unknown scan completeness must refuse.

findings.title: Generic ledger verifier accepts source as its own vault, directly or through a symlink
findings.explanation: Matching hashes alone do not prove an independent surviving copy. Vault verifier refuses source-equals-vault; generic verifier says SAFE and quarantine dry-run passes.
findings.recommendation: Bring generic ledger authorization into parity with the vault verifier's canonical source/vault separation checks.

findings.title: Directory ledger row without vault digest is accepted as preservation
findings.explanation: A three-field directory row has no vault_sha256. Generic verifier conditionally skips that hash and returns SAFE; vault verifier correctly refuses row-incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Require both complete lowercase SHA-256 fields before a directory receipt can authorize SAFE.

findings.title: Generic ledger verifier accepts a vault copy nested inside its removal target
findings.explanation: The source manifest and nested-vault manifest both match the ledger, but removing the source also removes the only vault copy. Vault verifier refuses vault-inside-source; generic verifier says SAFE.
findings.recommendation: Refuse a canonical vault destination equal to or contained by the canonical source directory.
